name: B.F. Skinner
shortBio: Pioneered radical behaviorism, operant conditioning, and reinforcement schedules; argued free will is an illusion and behavior is governed by environmental consequences.
centralQuestion: How do schedules of operant reinforcement select and shape complex human behavior without invoking autonomous inner agency?

keyWorks.title: The Behavior of Organisms
keyWorks.description: Establishes operant conditioning through experimental analysis of behavior.

keyWorks.title: Science and Human Behavior
keyWorks.description: Extends radical behaviorism to government, education, religion, and culture.

keyWorks.title: Beyond Freedom and Dignity
keyWorks.description: Critiques traditional concepts of autonomous human dignity in favor of behavioral technology.
